info.name: sandbox-runner
info.description: sandbox-runner HTTP + MCP endpoints. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable to switch between local (http://localhost:8012) and container-network (http://sandbox-runner:8000) targets. For LiteLLM pass-through, set baseUrl to http://localhost:4001/v1/sandbox and add an Authorization: Bearer sk-... header at the collection level. See ai/sandbox/ENDPOINTS.md for the full reference.

variable.description: Runner base URL. Localhost publish is 8012; on ai_shared it's http://sandbox-runner:8000.
12-char hex id returned by POST /run. Fill in after spawning to run the /jobs/{id} + DELETE requests.

request.description: Liveness + DB status. Returns {"status": "ok", "db": "up"} when the runner can reach sandbox-db; "degraded" / "down" otherwise. No auth.

Spawn a static HTML sandbox — nginx serves the files map at /. Returns { sandbox_id, url, expires_at }. The URL is reachable via sandbox-proxy at http://localhost:8011/{sandbox_id}/ from the host, or http://sandbox-proxy/{sandbox_id}/ from ai_shared.

body.raw:
{
  "runtime": "python",
  "files": {
    "app.py": "import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

st.title('sine wave demo')
n = st.slider('samples', 10, 500, 100)
freq = st.slider('frequency', 1, 10, 3)
x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n)
df = pd.DataFrame({'x': x, 'y': np.sin(freq * x)})
st.line_chart(df.set_index('x'))
"
  },
  "ttl_seconds": 900
}

request.description: Spawn a Streamlit sandbox. Runtime `python` base image has streamlit, gradio, flask, fastapi, pandas, numpy, matplotlib, plotly, requests, pillow pre-installed. Add a requirements.txt to files to install additional deps via sandbox-egress (pypi allowlisted). Cold-start ~2s pre-baked; 20-90s if pip install runs.

Illustrates the install-if-present pattern. If files contains a requirements.txt, the base image entrypoint runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` before executing the command. pip goes through HTTP_PROXY=sandbox-egress:8888 and hits the pypi.org / files.pythonhosted.org allowlist.

Spawn a Node sandbox. Base image has serve, vite, react, react-dom, express, next installed globally so `require('express')` works without a package.json. Add a package.json to files to trigger `npm install` on boot.
Multi-file Vite + React counter. Vite HMR uses WebSockets — sandbox-proxy (Caddy) forwards them by default, so buttons work end-to-end when iframed.

List every sandbox in the registry (running + terminal). Fixed limit of 20 in PostgresRegistry.list_all(). Ordered by updated_at DESC. Returns JobsListResponse — see ENDPOINTS.md for the JobBase shape. max_concurrent / available are null (the runner enforces its concurrency cap in-process, not in the registry).
Snapshot of one sandbox. 404 if unknown. Set the sandboxId collection variable to the id returned by POST /run first.
Tear a sandbox down early. Stops the container, removes it, deletes the row, releases the concurrency slot. Returns 204 no body. 404 if the sandbox id is unknown.

OpenAPI schema for the OpenWebUI Tool Server integration. Register the tool server in OpenWebUI Admin Panel → Settings → Tools → Add Connection with base URL {{baseUrl}}/tool — OpenWebUI GETs this schema at registration time.

OpenWebUI Rich-UI integration. Returns HTMLResponse with `Content-Disposition: inline` — OpenWebUI renders the response body (an `<iframe>` pointing at sandbox-proxy) as an embedded artifact under the tool call indicator, no model round-trip needed. Response Content-Type is text/html (not JSON). See ai/sandbox/ENDPOINTS.md § OpenWebUI Tool Server for details.

item.name: MCP
item.description: FastMCP JSON-RPC over HTTP. All requests are POST /mcp/ (trailing slash required — the runner responds to POST /mcp with 307 → /mcp/). Every client must send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` and start with `initialize`. FastMCP returns responses as SSE events by default; if you need a single JSON response, some clients unwrap the SSE frame automatically.

request.description: Handshake. Must be called first. Response body carries serverInfo (name = 'sandbox', version from FastMCP), protocolVersion, and capabilities. Response headers include `mcp-session-id` — copy it into subsequent calls' `Mcp-Session-Id` request header if your client doesn't handle sessions automatically.

header.description: Paste in the mcp-session-id header value returned by initialize.

request.description: Enumerate available tools. sandbox-runner exposes exactly one: preview_app.

Invoke preview_app via MCP. Same effect as POST /run but the model side of the world uses this shape. Result body has { url, sandbox_id, expires_at } wrapped in the JSON-RPC `result.content[0].text` per MCP tool-result spec.
Invoke preview_app for a Python (Streamlit) sandbox via MCP.
